title: Tic-tac-toe
description:
Write a two-player game of tic-tac-toe on a 3 × 3 board. Players type their moves as `row column` (each 1 to 3):

```
X to move: 2 2
 . | . | .
---+---+---
 . | X | .
---+---+---
 . | . | .
O to move: 1 1
 O | . | .
---+---+---
 . | X | .
---+---+---
 . | . | .
X to move: ...
```

Rules:
- `X` moves first; players alternate. Print `X to move: ` (or `O to move: `) before reading each line.
- A line that is not two whole numbers prints `Enter row and column, like 2 3`; numbers outside 1 to 3 print `Out of range`; a square that is already used prints `Taken`. After any of these, the same player tries again.
- After each valid move, print the board as shown: each row is ` a | b | c`, rows are separated by `---+---+---`, and empty squares are `.`.
- When a player gets three in a row (across, down or diagonally), print `X wins!` (or `O wins!`) and stop. When the board is full without a winner, print `Draw.` and stop.
- If the input ends before the game is over, print `Game abandoned.`
hints: Check rows and columns in one loop over `i`: row `i` is `b[i][0]`, `b[i][1]`, `b[i][2]`, and column `i` is `b[0][i]`, `b[1][i]`, `b[2][i]`. Then check the two diagonals.
Convert the player's 1-to-3 numbers to array indexes by subtracting 1.
requirements: Write separate methods for printing the board, checking for a winner, and checking whether the board is full.
stretch: Add a computer player for `O` that wins if it can, blocks `X` if it must, and otherwise takes the centre, a corner, or any square.
